title: NEW AQ: A Middle Path for Mexico
gist: AQ's editors summarize Vanessa Rubio-Marquez's cover story: Mexico should keep a steady middle path with the US, enforce red lines, and cut vulnerability via fiscal and Pemex reform, since 87% of its exports still enter the US duty-free.

themes.theme: Case for continuity with the US

insights.claim: Mexico has little choice for now but to continue its special relationship with the US, and Sheinbaum's decisions suggest her government concludes significant diversification would take decades if viable at all.
insights.speaker: AQ EDITORS
insights.so_what: Expect Mexico to avoid confrontation and not pivot trade; supports base case of policy continuity.

insights.claim: About 87% of Mexican exports still enter the US duty-free, and those facing tariffs average only 3.4%, versus 22% for China.
insights.speaker: AQ EDITORS
insights.so_what: Mexico retains a large relative tariff advantage, a pillar of the nearshoring thesis.
insights.quote: close to 87% of Mexican exports still enter duty-free, and those with tariffs have an average rate of just 3.4%—compared to 22% for China

insights.claim: Mexico is as exposed as arguably any country to US tariffs, sanctions and military-intervention threats, prompting debate about confronting Washington as Canada's Mark Carney has.
insights.speaker: AQ EDITORS
insights.so_what: Frames the policy fork Mexico is not taking.
insights.locator: For the better part of a decade

insights.claim: Mexico can reduce vulnerability by curbing its sizable fiscal deficit, including more transparent management and governance of Pemex.
insights.speaker: AQ EDITORS
insights.so_what: Pemex and fiscal reform are the watch items for sovereign-credit direction.

insights.claim: Pemex's financial debt was $77.5 billion at the end of June and it has struggled for years to reverse declining crude production.
insights.speaker: AQ EDITORS

insights.claim: Property taxes generate revenue equal to only 0.2% of GDP in Mexico; reform could push it closer to 3%.
insights.speaker: AQ EDITORS
insights.so_what: A large untapped fiscal lever if pursued.

insights.claim: Sheinbaum must keep enforcing red lines with Washington, such as a possible unilateral US military strike on a cartel target in Mexican territory.
insights.speaker: AQ EDITORS
insights.so_what: A unilateral US strike is a bilateral-relations tail risk.
